method: One run per fixture in a fresh temporary directory. Time each LuaLaTeX subprocess launched by the production _compile_latex helper; total_seconds covers all passes. The N=100 untagged variant changes only tagging=on to tagging=off in the temporary rendered source. No production files or settings are changed.

convergence_diagnostic.fixture: branching N=10, 22 people, 11 families, 33 events, 2 synthetic 96x72 portraits, tagging on
convergence_diagnostic.method: Capture book.aux, book.toc and book.out after each pass of the production _compile_latex helper; compare extracted text and Poppler structure output from saved pass PDFs.
convergence_diagnostic.interpretation: Do not ignore @tag@LastPage when checking convergence. The official tagpdf tree code uses the recorded tagstruct count to determine structure-ID padding and the recorded tagmcabs count to assemble the ParentTree; the third pass reads the counts produced after the table of contents has been tagged.

section_profile_diagnostic.fixture: branching N=100, 202 people, 101 families, 303 events, 20 synthetic 96x72 portraits, tagging on
section_profile_diagnostic.method: Instrument a single first LuaLaTeX pass in a temporary rendered source with expl3 benchmark tic/toc pairs around the seven book sections and retain tagpdf finalization timing hooks. Section intervals include page breaks and shipout between their start and next section marker.
section_profile_diagnostic.interpretation: Family connections, the documentary appendix and person profiles account for most measured section time; final tagpdf tree writing takes about 3.28 seconds in this pass. This single instrumented pass is diagnostic only and does not establish a stable performance budget or isolate the cost of individual LaTeX operations.

section_group_profile_diagnostic.fixture: branching N=100, 202 people, 101 families, 303 events, 20 synthetic 96x72 portraits, tagging on
section_group_profile_diagnostic.method: Instrument one first LuaLaTeX pass in a temporary source with benchmark tic/toc pairs around groups of 25 top-level family sections, profile subsections and citation entries.
section_group_profile_diagnostic.interpretation: The two groups of 25 child-bearing family sections take 10.90 seconds together and contain 200 parent-child links; the remaining 51 childless sections take about 2.50 seconds. This aligns with the extra nested relationship-list content, but the timers include page breaks and shipout and do not isolate the cost of those operations. Profile and citation groups have broadly even times.

target_encoding_diagnostic.fixture: branching N=100, 202 people, 101 families, 303 events, 20 prepared synthetic 96x72 portraits, tagging on
target_encoding_diagnostic.method: Compile paired target-label variants through the production _compile_latex helper in fresh temporary directories. The compact variant changes only the internal target-name encoding from UTF-8 hex to padding-free lowercase RFC 4648 base32. Repeat the pair with the execution order reversed.
target_encoding_diagnostic.interpretation: Across two paired runs, base32 target labels reduce the median complete compile time by 8.77% and source size by 141755 bytes. The produced PDFs retain the same page count, tagged status, named-destination count, structure output and extracted text; the final PDF grows by about 0.56%. This is a two-pair local benchmark, not a statistical performance budget.
target_encoding_diagnostic.source_size_note: The earlier N=100 source-size figure of 1249510 bytes matches rendering the model before media derivatives are prepared. These paired runs measure the prepared source actually compiled, at 1265310 bytes for hex labels.

page_link_macro_diagnostic.fixture: branching N=100, 202 people, 101 families, 303 events, 20 prepared synthetic 96x72 portraits, tagging on
page_link_macro_diagnostic.method: Factor the repeated page-reference source into a LaTeX macro that expands to the same two hyperlinks and page reference. Run the production benchmark twice in fresh temporary directories. Compare with the two base32 runs above; LuaHBTeX is the same, while the Python runtime differs.
page_link_macro_diagnostic.interpretation: The macro cuts generated source by 26.86% and sampled temporary workspace peak by about 10.16%. The two-run median compile time is effectively unchanged from the base32 reference; this source compaction does not provide a measured runtime improvement. PDF size, page count, tagged status, named destinations, structure output and extracted text remain equivalent.

comparison.reason: Poppler reports Tagged: no for the untagged diagnostic PDF. The experiment points to substantial time spent in tagged compilation, but disabling tagging loses the PDF structure required by the project.
